content: {"like": ["The music score was praised as a positive element.", "The casting of Sinead O'Connor as Emily Brontë herself was highlighted as interesting.", "The film’s lack of excessive stage‑like production was seen as a plus.", "Certain performances—Jeremy Northam as Hindley, Janet McTeer as Ellen \"Nelly\" Dean, and Jason Riddington as Hareton—were described as the saving grace of the film."], "dislike": ["The film was considered overrated and not authentic to the novel’s essence.", "The house representing Wuthering Heights was described as fake and the locations did not fit the novel’s description.", "Actors were deemed too old and miscast, notably Ralph Fiennes as Heathcliff and Juliette Binoche as Catherine Earnshaw/Linton.", "Binoche’s French accent and the distracting blonde wig for the younger Catherine were criticized.", "Several characters were portrayed as weak or colorless, such as Edgar Linton and the sickly Linton Earnshaw.", "Hindley was seen as under‑used and the film was suggested to have benefited from a different casting choice.", "Budget constraints were noted in costuming, hair (wigs), and interiors, which detracted from the overall quality.", "The film’s attempts to cover more of the book were seen as falling short compared to earlier adaptations." ]}
